clue.text: Inexpensive company car that’s dilapidated inside

indicators.note: one thing sitting inside another means its letters go within the other word

blocks.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company
a heap is slang for a dilapidated old car

explanation.surface: A company car so cheap it is falling apart on the inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dilapidated' belongs with 'car' to give a decrepit vehicle, a heap, which then goes inside the company abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapo is informal for something bought cheaply, a low-cost or bargain item, so it fits as an adjective.

clue.text: Communicates with diplomacy amongst Tories

indicators.note: being amongst others means placed in the middle of them, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: Cons is short for Conservatives, the Tories
tact is diplomacy in handling people

explanation.surface: Someone liaising tactfully within the Conservative party.
explanation.definitionFit: To contact someone is to get in touch, so a verb meaning gets in touch with matches the phrase.

clue.text: Wood seen in reversing Daimler

indicators.note: something seen in a word is visible inside its letters, already present in the text
reversing a car takes it backwards, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the three middle letters of the car make, which read backwards give the tree

explanation.surface: A wooden panel noticed in a Daimler car as it backs up.
explanation.walkthrough: Daimler is a British luxury car make; read it backwards and ELM sits in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm is a hardwood timber from the tree of that name, a type of wood used in furniture.

clue.text: Nobody spots a conclusion to deadlock around flipping EU question

indicators.note: something flipping around is turned over end to end, so these letters run backwards
the conclusion of a word is its very end, so only its final letter is used

blocks.note: pips are the spots on dice or dominoes
EU as written plus Q, the abbreviation for question
taken as written
the final letter

explanation.surface: A political story about breaking a deadlock over a European Union question.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's 'around' is loose: the turned EU question simply sits between the spots and the final pair of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobody is an insignificant person, and pipsqueak is a dismissive name for someone small and unimportant.

clue.text: Budge had fine one back in thirty-four

definitions.text: Budge had fine one back in thirty-four

blocks.clueFragment: Budge had fine one back in thirty-four
blocks.note: surface reading: someone shifting, or a fine one returned in some event
setter's reading: Don Budge, the American tennis champion of the 1930s, had a fine tennis stroke in those years

explanation.surface: An odd little sentence about budging and something fine coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: Budge is Don Budge, a tennis great of the 1930s, famed above all for his backhand; 'back' teases that stroke, but the 4-across answer is the stroke played on the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: A forehand is the tennis stroke played with the palm facing forward, one a champion player would hit well.

clue.text: Function for each one in sorties regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
one part placed in another sits inside its letters

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
per means for each, as in per person
a means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: Military talk of each pilot's role on bombing sorties.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to work or run, so the verb meaning to work properly fits function.

clue.text: Former Liberal coming round to praise

indicators.note: coming round something means encircling it, so these letters wrap the other word

blocks.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ex-Liberal politician being won round to applause.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to laud or speak highly of something, a verb synonym for praise.

clue.text: Mass of things coming from Malta George Cross

indicators.note: cross can mean angry or worked up, a state in which things get jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written: eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Malta's George Cross, awarded to the whole island in 1942, seems to be the subject.
explanation.walkthrough: The George Cross is a British gallantry medal; Malta received it collectively for wartime courage, so 'George Cross' reads as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An agglomerate is a collection or cluster of things lumped together, a jumbled heap.

clue.text: What I’d refuse to acknowledge is some yarn?

blocks.note: first meaning: what I would be if I refused to admit something, one who denies
second meaning: a unit measuring the fineness of yarn, as with stockings

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is 'what I'd be if I refused to acknowledge'; the second is the textile unit, pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: One who denies things is a denier, while a denier is also the weight measure for silk, nylon or yarn thickness.

clue.text: Small number abroad primarily supporting C&A chain

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the letters of the store name
ten is a small number
its first letter

explanation.surface: A small overseas branch backing the C&A clothing store chain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' means placed underneath, so the wordplay before it comes last. C&A is a high-street clothing chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Catena is the Latin word for chain, used in English for a connected series or linked sequence.

clue.text: What may be attached to door handle’s helping

definitions.text: What may be attached to door

blocks.note: a handle is slang for a name
a plate is a helping or plateful of food

explanation.surface: A door handle, with something helping it work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'door handle' looks like a single object, but door belongs to the definition and handle starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A nameplate is a small plaque bearing someone's name, often fixed to an office or house entrance.

clue.text: Hybrid rhino found around Indian state? Not quite!

indicators.note: not quite means falling a little short, so the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A cross-bred rhinoceros turning up in India.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhino is not the animal but old slang for money, as is tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigon is the offspring of a male tiger and a lioness, a cross-bred big cat.

clue.text: Long-standing worker’s irritation after parking withdrawn

indicators.note: something withdrawn is taken away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a worker ant; the 's means 'has'
pique is irritation or resentment
P is the abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A veteran employee annoyed at losing a parking space.
explanation.definitionFit: Antique means very old or of great age, so it works as an adjective for something lasting from long ago.

clue.text: Char I’d brought round longing for a whiteboard?

definitions.note: an example, hence the question mark

indicators.note: brought round something means placed so as to encircle it, so these letters enclose another word

blocks.note: char is British slang for tea
taken as written without the apostrophe
aching means longing, as in an aching desire

explanation.surface: Someone craving tea while working at a whiteboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Char is the outer pair joined together, and the longing slips in after just two letters, not at the join.
explanation.definitionFit: A whiteboard is one classroom tool used by instructors, an example of equipment that helps lessons.

clue.text: Somehow glean nothing left? Right!

indicators.note: somehow means by some unspecified means, so the letters are arranged in some new way

blocks.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A gleaner finds nothing remaining in the field, and agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue works as the definition: after gleaning there is nothing left, 'Right!' confirming it is all gone.
explanation.definitionFit: All gone means completely used up or finished, so nothing remains, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Could be gents clever with IATA after tons lost

definitions.text: Could be gents clever with IATA after tons lost

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might become something else once rearranged
something lost is no longer there, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written; 'with' joins the two parts
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: Smart men working with the airline trade body after the loss of a lot of business.
explanation.walkthrough: IATA is the International Air Transport Association, which accredits ticket sellers, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Businesses that book flights and holidays for customers are often IATA-accredited, so clever gents allied with it describe such firms.

clue.text: NCO conserving last of explosive material

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter is taken

its final letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'explosive material' looks like a single phrase, but material is the definition. NCO is a non-commissioned officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporeal means bodily or physical, having substance, which is the adjective sense of material.

clue.text: Excitable star does like some chocolates

indicators.note: an excitable thing jumps about wildly, so these letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A highly strung celebrity enjoys a box of chocolates.
explanation.definitionFit: A box of assorted chocolates holds a mixture of varieties, so the adjective describes such sweets.

clue.text: Will they always support region in tremors near farm enclosures?

indicators.note: in places one word within the letters of another

clue.text: Deputy who evidently doesn’t stand out

blocks.note: first meaning: a substitute who takes someone's place

clue.text: Do please pass

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to pass or elapse as it goes by, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Youngster getting about in holiday island

clue.text: Ambassador stopping odd drips from the nose

clue.text: Viagra vendor has the answer where man’s lifeless down below.

clue.text: What some roads can be very near Land’s End
